papers.title: Human organotypic skin explant culture (hOSEC): an alternative approach to Staphylococcus aureus colonization assays.
papers.authorString: Lisboa LFT, Barbosa LD, Giarola F, Galani LC, da Costa WP, Frade MAC, Monteiro MC, Lima FR.
papers.journalTitle: International microbiology : the official journal of the Spanish Society for Microbiology
papers.abstractText: hOSEC provides a relevant ex vivo platform to study Staphylococcus aureus infection, preserving the structural and immune components of human skin while reducing animal use. This pilot study aimed to standardize hOSEC for S. aureus colonization and infection, supporting translational research and novel therapeutic approaches, compared to other models in offering a cost-effective platform. hOSEC was established from surgical samples (N = 06) using dermatological punch biopsies. Tissue viability was assessed by TTC assay. Staphylococcus aureus ATCC® 25923™ (susceptible), ATCC® BAA-1026™ and NCTC 12,493™ (resistant) strains were isolated and cultured. Infection assays were performed by epidermal colonization and intradermal inoculation, followed by bacterial curve analysis (CFU counts). Antimicrobial treatments were applied, and efficacy was evaluated through quantitative bacteriological analysis. The hOSEC model maintained structural integrity and mitochondrial activity throughout the study. Explants exposed retained high viability across antibiotic treatments (97.0%) and in untreated controls (98.0%). Intradermal inoculation (skin infection model) with 10⁶ CFU/mL led to bacterial proliferation (> 1 × 10⁸ CFU/mL) in untreated explants, while antibiotic-treated tissues showed strong suppression (average 2 × 10² CFU/mL). During epidermal colonization with wound and resistant strain, saline-treated explants maintained high bacterial counts: >10⁸ CFU/mL at 0-6 h, 4.5 × 104 CFU/mL at 12 h (p = 0.002), and persisted longer but were significantly reduced by antibiotic treatment (from 1 × 10⁸ CFU/mL at 0-6 h to 2 CFU/mL at 24 h). Notably, viable bacteria were still detectable in explants for up to 7 days (2.5 × 102 CFU/mL). Histopathological analysis revealed tissue damage characterized by acantholysis, necrosis, and apoptosis. The hOSEC model preserved tissue viability under bacterial inoculation and antibiotic exposure, supporting its use for ex vivo antimicrobial testing. Although intradermal inoculation (skin infection model) maintained high bacterial viability and effectively modeled deep tissue infection, injury-associated colonization (skin wound model) provided better spatial control of the infectious site by restricting bacterial growth to the injury area. Additionally, it was possible to identify histopathological alterations induced by bacterial infection, as histopathological analysis revealed acantholysis, necrosis, and apoptosis. These results demonstrate the model's utility for evaluating antibiotic penetration, local efficacy, and bacterial dynamics in controlled human skin-mimetic conditions.

papers.title: TREM-1 in Sepsis and Septic Shock: From Pathophysiology to Precision Immunomodulation.
papers.authorString: Evrard B, Van Der Poll T, Chousterman B, François B.
papers.journalTitle: Seminars in respiratory and critical care medicine
papers.abstractText: Sepsis remains one of the leading causes of death worldwide, and decades of immunomodulatory trials targeting inflammation have failed to improve outcomes, largely because of the biological heterogeneity of the host response. Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells-1 (TREM-1) has emerged as a particularly relevant pathway in this context: rather than initiating pathogen recognition, TREM-1 amplifies signals generated by pattern-recognition receptors, acting as a rheostat that fine-tunes the magnitude of the innate immune response to promote antimicrobial defense while limiting inflammation-induced tissue injury. Both insufficient and excessive activation of this pathway have been associated with adverse outcomes in experimental and clinical studies. Soluble TREM-1 (sTREM-1), released proportionally to pathway activation, has been extensively investigated as a biomarker of infection and disease severity. Its diagnostic performance is moderate and best interpreted alongside clinical and microbiological data, but its prognostic value is more consistent, particularly when assessed serially or combined with complementary host-response markers. More recently, sTREM-1 has been explored as a theranostic biomarker to guide pathway-directed treatment. Nangibotide, the most clinically advanced TREM-1 inhibitor, has demonstrated feasibility and short-term safety across phase 1 and phase 2 trials, but has not yet met its primary efficacy endpoint in an unselected population; exploratory analyses suggest that treatment benefit may be concentrated among patients with the highest baseline sTREM-1 concentrations, a hypothesis that remains to be prospectively validated. This review summarizes the biology of the TREM-1 pathway, the clinical evidence supporting sTREM-1 as a diagnostic, prognostic, and theranostic biomarker, and the current state of TREM-1-targeted therapeutics. It also discusses what the clinical development of nangibotide illustrates about the hope and the difficulty of precision immunomodulation in sepsis.

papers.title: Rapid enhancement of antibiotic resistance and divergent remodeling of gene expression in single cells of bacteria
papers.authorString: Umetani M, Hashimoto M, Akiyoshi S, Okura R, Sakata N, Kotani H, Kussell E, Furusawa C, Wakamoto Y.
papers.abstractText: Exposing bacterial cell populations to antibiotics often results in the emergence of descendants with enhanced resistance. Phenotypic heterogeneity and global physiological responses are thought to contribute to resistance evolution. However, identifying the specific stages of drug exposure where phenotypic heterogeneity and physiological responses play critical roles remains elusive. Using long-term single-cell lineage tracking of an Escherichia coli resistance model, here we reveal that resistance-enhanced cells emerge rapidly within a few generations in a clonal bacterial cell population under chloramphenicol (Cp) exposure and stably transmit the enhanced resistance for hundreds of generations in the presence of Cp. High expression of a resistance protein was advantageous during the initial period of drug exposure, but conferred only a marginal fitness advantage during the period of resistance enhancement. Transcriptomic profiles of resistance-enhanced cell populations were lineage-specific, suggesting that multiple gene expression states can support enhanced resistance. Altogether, these results suggest that an interplay between initial phenotypic heterogeneity and divergent remodeling of gene expression drives the rapid acquisition of enhanced antibiotic resistance.

papers.title: Single-cell multi-omic landscape reveals anatomical-specific immune features in adult and pediatric sepsis.
papers.authorString: Ye Q, Lai X, Liu Y, Zhang Z, Fu Y, Luo J, Liu C, Duan J, Ding H, Liu Y, Ao Z, Tao Y, Ai S, Huang W, Jiang L, Liu Y, Xu F, Cao J.
papers.abstractText: The anatomical source of infection is a major determinant of sepsis outcomes; however, how distinct sites shape immunity remains unclear. Here we applied multi-omic profiling, integrating single-cell transcriptomics, single-cell T cell receptor and B cell receptor sequencing, CITE-seq, bulk RNA sequencing and plasma proteomics, to analyze peripheral blood mononuclear cells and plasma from 281 adult and pediatric individuals with sepsis and controls. We identified an NR4A2+ central memory CD4+ T cell subset enriched in abdominal, pulmonary and skin sepsis, with features of exhaustion; genetic perturbations showed Nr4a2 loss improved survival, while overexpression worsened it. Proinflammatory CD8+ T, natural killer and natural killer T subsets expressing CCL4, CCL3 and tumor necrosis factor expanded in adult abdominal and pulmonary sepsis, while pediatric pulmonary sepsis featured proliferative CD14+ monocytes, findings validated in external single-cell cohorts and confirmed in 164 independent individuals. Plasma proteomics revealed shared mediators including interleukin-6 and EN-RAGE across anatomical sites and ages. Together, our findings delineate anatomical-specific and age-specific immune programs in sepsis, highlighting candidate targets for precision immunotherapy.

analysis.design: 281 名成人与儿童脓毒症患者及对照；整合 PBMC 单细胞转录组、TCR/BCR、CITE-seq、bulk RNA-seq 与血浆蛋白组。
analysis.finding: 研究聚焦感染解剖来源如何塑造成人与儿童的免疫特征；具体分层结果应以论文正文和图表核验。
analysis.caveat: 多组学整合队列；横断面关联不能单独证明因果。阅读时核对各组样本量、感染部位定义和验证队列。

papers.title: Bacterial droplet-based single-cell RNA-seq reveals antibiotic-associated heterogeneous cellular states.
papers.authorString: Ma P, Amemiya HM, He LL, Gandhi SJ, Nicol R, Bhattacharyya RP, Smillie CS, Hung DT.
papers.abstractText: We introduce BacDrop, a highly scalable technology for bacterial single-cell RNA sequencing that has overcome many challenges hindering the development of scRNA-seq in bacteria. BacDrop can be applied to thousands to millions of cells from both gram-negative and gram-positive species. It features universal ribosomal RNA depletion and combinatorial barcodes that enable multiplexing and massively parallel sequencing. We applied BacDrop to study Klebsiella pneumoniae clinical isolates and to elucidate their heterogeneous responses to antibiotic stress. In an unperturbed population presumed to be homogeneous, we found within-population heterogeneity largely driven by the expression of mobile genetic elements that promote the evolution of antibiotic resistance. Under antibiotic perturbation, BacDrop revealed transcriptionally distinct subpopulations associated with different phenotypic outcomes including antibiotic persistence. BacDrop thus can capture cellular states that cannot be detected by bulk RNA-seq, which will unlock new microbiological insights into bacterial responses to perturbations and larger bacterial communities such as the microbiome.

analysis.design: 细菌液滴式单细胞 RNA 测序方法研究；BacDrop 用于观察抗生素相关的细胞状态异质性。
analysis.finding: 论文提出 BacDrop，并展示细菌群体在抗生素相关条件下存在转录状态异质性。
analysis.caveat: 重点是方法能力与特定实验条件下的状态异质性；不要直接外推为临床耐药机制。
